text:
Alex: hi all, onboarding question — i can SSH to bastion but `kubectl get pods` against dev cluster fails with DNS lookup error; `kubectl` is configured to talk to api.dev.cluster.internal. anyone seen this?
Priya: welcome Alex! quick check: can you nslookup api.dev.cluster.internal from your laptop while connected to corp-vpn?
Alex: `nslookup api.dev.cluster.internal` returns `server can't find api.dev.cluster.internal: NXDOMAIN`
Alex: but on the bastion `nslookup api.dev.cluster.internal` returns the cluster IP.
Ryan: likely split-tunnel + internal DNS not pushed to client. Our WireGuard profile only pushes routes, not DNS, for onboarding group.
Alex: hmm — i do see the dev VPC route when i run `route -n` but DNS seems off.
Priya: two quick options: 1) use an SSH SOCKS proxy via the bastion and set your KUBECONFIG to use the proxy, or 2) add an entry to /etc/hosts temporarily (if the cluster ip is stable). Which do you prefer?
Alex: i'd rather not touch /etc/hosts. How do i do the SOCKS proxy?
Priya: run `ssh -D 1080 ubuntu@bastion.company` then set `all_proxy=socks5h://localhost:1080` and export that env before running `kubectl`. Example:
```
$ ssh -D 1080 ubuntu@bastion.company -N
$ export ALL_PROXY=socks5h://localhost:1080
$ kubectl --context=dev get pods
```
Alex: ok tried that — `kubectl` still complains about certificate/host mismatch because the client resolves the API server name to public ip.
Priya: add `socks5h` forces DNS over the proxy, but some tools ignore ALL_PROXY. Another quick command: use curl via proxy to test DNS:
```
$ curl -x socks5h://localhost:1080 https://api.dev.cluster.internal:6443/healthz -k
```
Alex: curl over socks works and returns `ok`. so proxy is fine.
Ryan: long term we're going to push internal DNS to the onboarding split-tunnel group, but security needs to greenlight exposing resolver. Priya, can you open a ticket?
Priya: infra-bot, open INFRA-4999 to add internal DNS and VPC CIDRs to onboarding split-tunnel profile, assign to @Priya and request security review.
infra-bot: Created INFRA-4999: "onboarding: include internal DNS + VPC routes for WireGuard profile" assigned to @Priya. SLA: 72h.
Alex: thanks! any interim advice for kubectl?
Priya: you can set `server` in your kubeconfig to the bastion-forwarded hostname: add a port-forward via bastion: `ssh -L 6443:api.dev.cluster.internal:6443 ubuntu@bastion.company` then point kubeconfig server to `https://localhost:6443`. That preserves certs if you also add the cluster CA to your kubeconfig.
Alex: port-forward approach worked, pods list visible. appreciate the help 
Ryan: welcome aboard. Ping here if INFRA-4999 stalls.
Alex: will do, thanks everyone :tada:
